Resolves #17889

🌿 A drag that wanders into an iframe can no longer go silent and never end.

One Pointer Events sensor, `src/main/draggable/sensor/Pointer.mjs`, replaces the Mouse and Touch sensors. It hears `pointerdown`, `pointermove`, `pointerup` and `pointercancel`, owns each gesture by `pointerId`, and calls `setPointerCapture` on `documentElement` only once the drag starts past its threshold. A below-threshold click stays a click, and the pre-threshold iframe shield stays in place.

Because capture makes events name the document root, the sensor adds `eventPath` (the hit-test path), and `DragDrop` builds `target`, `targetPath` and the drop path from it. Mouse and pen coordinates are floored exactly as Chromium floors its compatibility mouse events; touch keeps its precision.

These stay unchanged:
- the device flags and the `mouseSensor` / `getMouseSensor()` aliases;
- the native-drag partition;
- the gating and `neo-drag-active`;
- the touch thresholds.

The port is rebuilt on current `dev`, so the later pressed-element cleanup, press-origin recovery, cross-window Escape and park-surface removal all hold.

Evidence: L3 (real-Chrome component and e2e runs, iframe crossing with trusted input) → L3 required (AC-2, AC-4). Residual: manual touch on a real device; the operator's drag walk is the merge gate.

agent-preflight: not hosted here; the baseline jobs run in CI.

| AC-3 | CI-covered: `pointercancel`, a second press of the same pointer and a lost release all end through one path with exactly one `drag:end` (unit arms plus a CDP `touchCancel` component arm). |

Hosted CI re-runs the reachable tiers at this head. Touch is checked through CDP emulation only. |
| AC-5 | `touch-action: none` is set on `.neo-splitter`, the `.neo-resizable` handles and the draggable dialog header (the dock splitter and stack handle already had it). The sensor README documents the capture window, the coordinate rule and the touch model. |

## Deltas from ticket
- **A seventh consumer, commit `11a3d6a5f2`:** raw synthetic mouse sequences sent through `EventSimulator#dispatch` would have stopped arming drags, with no error. That affects the Neural Link's `simulate_event`, the Workstation tour's gesture drivers, the Demo B drivers and `WorkstationGridRepaintNL`. A simulated `mousedown`, `mousemove` or `mouseup` now sends its pointer event first, as real input does. It's kept on purpose: dropping it would break every automated gesture silently.
- **Coordinate flooring:** Pointer Events carry fractional coordinates, which turned `WorkstationNestedColumnResizeNL` red mid-run (it aims at a pane edge). Flooring mouse and pen like Chromium's compatibility events fixed it.
- **The old `touchend` preventDefault is not ported.** After a drag the click lands on `html` under capture, so the worker no longer receives it.

## Test Evidence
- Iframe witness, red-first: 0 moves arrive inside the iframe on `dev`; on this branch moves stream and end exactly once.
- e2e: 50 files and 136 tests, run serially and all passed (local, Bridge on a non-fleet port).
- Pre-existing on `dev`, not caused here: in the DockSplitter component page, the dashboard container keeps `neo-is-dragging` for over 6 s after a splitter drag. That is the worker's SortZone session; the sensor sends its single `drag:end`. Noted for a pre-cut fix.

## Post-Merge Validation
- [ ] The operator's manual drag walk: dock tab drag and tear-out, splitter, column resize and reorder, the calendar event drag, and touch on a real device if one is at hand.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

- **Challenge**:
  1. **Synthetic `EventSimulator` moves/releases when `hasCapture === false` (`src/main/draggable/sensor/Pointer.mjs:522-524`):** In `Pointer#triggerStream`, `detail.eventPath = me.getHitTestPath(target)` is gated on `if (me.hasCapture && target)`. For synthetic gestures driven via `EventSimulator#driveDrag`, `setPointerCapture(2147483647)` throws `NotFoundError`, leaving `me.hasCapture === false`, while `driveDrag` dispatches `pointermove` and `pointerup` on `'document.body'`. Consequently, `DragDrop#getEventData` falls back to `e.targetPath = e.path` (`[body, html, document, window]`) instead of the hit-tested `target` path at `(clientX, clientY)`. This matches retired `Mouse.mjs` behavior and all current `driveDrag` suites pass because they read coordinates or `DragCoordinator` geometry rather than `data.targetPath` / `isDrop`, but if a future `driveDrag` spec targets a `dropZoneIdentifier` or calendar column via `data.targetPath`, populating `detail.eventPath` whenever `target && event.target !== target` (or unconditionally when `target` is non-null) would give synthetic `driveDrag` moves the same hit-test path as captured native moves.
  2. **Root-cause trace for the pre-existing `DockSplitter` `neo-is-dragging` note (`test/playwright/component/dashboard/DockSplitterIframePane.spec.mjs:359-361`):** Tracing why the standalone `dashboard` in `DockSplitterIframePane.spec.mjs` retains `neo-is-dragging` after a splitter drag confirms it is orthogonal to `Pointer.mjs`. In that fixture, `DockSplitter` (`baseCls: ['neo-dashboard-dock-splitter', 'neo-draggable']`) is mounted as a direct child of `Neo.dashboard.Container` (`dragResortable: true`). Because `Splitter` registers its `drag:start` DOM listener without `bubble: false` (`src/component/Splitter.mjs:94-97`) and `container.DragZone#isDraggableItem` / `container.SortZone#isDraggableItem` (`src/draggable/container/DragZone.mjs:84`, `SortZone.mjs:309`) do not exclude `Splitter` items (`Splitter#isSplitterItem`), `drag:start` bubbles from `splitter` to `dashboard.sortZone`, which treats the splitter as a sortable widget, stamps `neo-is-dragging` on `dashboard`, and starts an async proxy/placeholder mount while `splitter.dragZone` claims `DragDrop.dragZoneId` on the Main thread. Excluding splitters in `container.DragZone#isDraggableItem` (or setting `bubble: false` on `Splitter`'s `drag:start`/`drag:end` listeners) will cleanly close that pre-cut follow-up.
